```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Títulos de productos únicos por bloque
prods_b1 <- unique(df_raw$i[1:150000])
prods_b2 <- unique(df_raw$i[150001:250000])

# 1. ¿Cuántos productos del Bloque 2 son conocidos (aparecieron en B1)?
conocidos_b2 <- sum(prods_b2 %in% prods_b1)
total_prods_b2 <- length(prods_b2)

# 2. Resumen de solapamiento
tibble(
  total_productos_b2 = total_prods_b2,
  reaparecen_en_b1   = conocidos_b2,
  nuevos_en_b2       = total_prods_b2 - conocidos_b2,
  pct_conocidos      = round((conocidos_b2 / total_prods_b2) * 100, 2)
)
```


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

# ==============================================================================
# AUDITORÍA ESTRUCTURAL Y LIMPIEZA DEL DATASET
# ==============================================================================
# Contexto del dominio: E-commerce (transacciones con título de producto en 'i').
#
# 1. Columna '...1': No es un ID de usuario ni de ítem; es el índice autonumérico
#    de pandas generado al concatenar dos dataframes sin resetear índice.
# 2. Bloque 2 (filas 150k a 250k): Conjunto de test sin etiquetas válidas 
#    ('fraude' imputado artificialmente en 0%).
# 3. Columna 'i': Título del producto vendido. Su distribución de cola pesada
#    refleja productos más populares con múltiples ventas independientes.
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Demostración empírica del problema
auditoria <- tibble(
  secuencia_b1_autonumerica = all(df_raw[[1]][1:150000] == 0:149999),
  secuencia_b2_autonumerica = all(df_raw[[1]][150001:250000] == 0:99999),
  tasa_fraude_b1_train      = mean(df_raw$fraude[1:150000]),
  tasa_fraude_b2_dummy      = mean(df_raw$fraude[150001:250000])
)

print(auditoria)

# 2. Descarte de observaciones sin target y remoción del índice residual
df_limpio <- df_raw %>%
  slice(1:150000) %>%
  select(-1)

# 3. Control de aserciones de integridad
stopifnot(
  nrow(df_limpio) == 150000,
  round(mean(df_limpio$fraude), 2) == 0.05,
  sum(is.na(df_limpio$i)) == 0
)

cat(sprintf(
  "Dataset listo: 150.000 transacciones válidas | %d productos distintos en 'i' | Fraude: %.2f%%\n",
  n_distinct(df_limpio$i),
  mean(df_limpio$fraude) * 100
))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Vector de la variable k (limpio de NA si los hubiera)
k_vec <- df_limpio$k[!is.na(df_limpio$k)]

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PARÁMETROS EMPÍRICOS BÁSICOS VS. TEÓRICOS U(0, 1)
# ==============================================================================
# Para U(0, 1):
#   Mínimo = 0, Máximo = 1
#   Media = 0.5, Varianza = 1/12 ≈ 0.08333 (Desvío estándar ≈ 0.28867)
# ==============================================================================

metricas_empiricas <- tibble(
  minimo      = min(k_vec),
  q25         = quantile(k_vec, 0.25),
  mediana     = median(k_vec),
  media       = mean(k_vec),
  q75         = quantile(k_vec, 0.75),
  maximo      = max(k_vec),
  desvio_std  = sd(k_vec),
  n_valores   = length(k_vec)
)

print(metricas_empiricas)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. TEST DE BONDAD DE AJUSTE (KOLMOGOROV-SMIRNOV)
# ==============================================================================
# H0: La muestra proviene de una distribución U(0, 1).
# Si p-valor < 0.05, se rechaza formalmente la hipótesis de uniformidad.
# ==============================================================================

ks_resultado <- ks.test(k_vec, "punif", min = 0, max = 1)
print(ks_resultado)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. DIAGNÓSTICO VISUAL: HISTOGRAMA Y QQ-PLOT
# ==============================================================================

# Histograma con la densidad teórica esperada (línea horizontal en y = 1)
p1 <- ggplot(data.frame(k = k_vec), aes(x = k)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Densidad Empírica de k vs. Densidad Teórica U(0, 1)",
    subtitle = "La línea roja discontinua representa la función de densidad f(x) = 1",
    x = "k",
    y = "Densidad"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# QQ-Plot contra la distribución uniforme
p2 <- ggplot(data.frame(k = k_vec), aes(sample = k)) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qunif, dparams = list(min = 0, max = 1), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qunif, dparams = list(min = 0, max = 1), color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Q-Q Plot de k contra U(0, 1)",
    x = "Cuantiles Teóricos U(0, 1)",
    y = "Cuantiles Empíricos"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)
print(p2)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# AUDITORÍA DE 'es_madrugada' Y TASA DE FRAUDE POR HORA (UTC VS LOCAL)
# ==============================================================================
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

df_limpio <- df_limpio %>%
  mutate(
    hora_utc   = hour(fecha),
    hora_local = hour(with_tz(fecha, "America/Buenos_Aires")),
    fecha_dia  = as.Date(fecha),
    es_madrugada_opt = (hora_utc >= 23 | hora_utc <= 5),
    es_principal = if_else(g %in% c("BR", "AR"), "Principal (BR/AR)", "No Principal (Otros)")
  )

tasa_hora <- df_limpio %>%
  group_by(hora = hora_utc) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    n_fraude    = sum(fraude),
    tasa_fraude = mean(fraude),
    se          = sqrt(tasa_fraude * (1 - tasa_fraude) / n),
    ic_inf      = pmax(0, tasa_fraude - 1.96 * se),
    ic_sup      = tasa_fraude + 1.96 * se,
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(es_madrugada = (hora >= 23 | hora <= 5))

tasa_global <- mean(df_limpio$fraude)

p_tasa <- ggplot(tasa_hora, aes(x = factor(hora), y = tasa_fraude)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = es_madrugada), alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ic_inf, ymax = ic_sup), width = 0.25, color = "gray30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tasa_global, linetype = "dashed", color = "red3", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 12, y = tasa_global + 0.008, 
           label = paste0("Tasa promedio: ", percent(tasa_global, accuracy = 0.1)),
           color = "red3", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#2b5c8f", "TRUE" = "#e6550d"),
                    labels = c("Día / Tarde", "es_madrugada optimizada (23h - 05h UTC)"),
                    name = "Ventana") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.21)) +
  labs(title = "Tasa de Fraude por Hora (UTC)",
       subtitle = "Riesgo concentrado entre las 23h (9.0%) y las 05h (7.2%), con pico a las 02h (17.2%)",
       x = "Hora (UTC)", y = "Tasa de Fraude") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_volumen <- ggplot(tasa_hora, aes(x = factor(hora), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "gray50", alpha = 0.75, width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format()) +
  labs(title = "Volumen de Transacciones por Hora (UTC)",
       x = "Hora (UTC)", y = "Cantidad de Transacciones") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_tasa / p_volumen
```

df_no_principales <- df_limpio %>%
  filter(!g %in% c("BR", "AR")) %>%
  mutate(
    g_etiqueta = fct_na_value_to_level(g, level = "Missing / NA"),

# Resumen general de países no principales
df_no_principales %>%
  group_by(g_etiqueta) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_total = percent(n / nrow(df_limpio), accuracy = 0.01),
    tasa_fraude = percent(mean(fraude), accuracy = 0.1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  head(10)

# Serie temporal diaria por país no principal

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85, alpha = 0.9) +

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# ANÁLISIS DE RÁFAGAS TEMPORALES DE PRODUCTOS REPETIDOS (BURST / VELOCITY)
# ==============================================================================
df_burst <- df_limpio %>%
  arrange(fecha) %>%
  group_by(i) %>%
  mutate(
    fecha_prev_i = lag(fecha),
    delta_sec_i  = as.numeric(difftime(fecha, fecha_prev_i, units = "secs"))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    ventana_rafaga = case_when(
      is.na(delta_sec_i)   ~ "1. Primera vez visto (Sin historia)",
      delta_sec_i <= 600   ~ "2. Menos de 10 minutos (Ráfaga extrema)",
      delta_sec_i <= 3600  ~ "3. Entre 10 min y 1 hora",
      delta_sec_i <= 86400 ~ "4. Entre 1 hora y 24 horas",
      TRUE                 ~ "5. Más de 24 horas"
    )
  )

tasa_global_fraude <- mean(df_burst$fraude)

resumen_rafaga <- df_burst %>%
  group_by(ventana_rafaga) %>%
  summarise(
    total_tx    = n(),
    pct_pob     = percent(total_tx / nrow(df_burst), accuracy = 0.01),
    tx_fraude   = sum(fraude),
    tasa_fraude = mean(fraude),
    lift        = tasa_fraude / tasa_global_fraude,
    se          = sqrt(tasa_fraude * (1 - tasa_fraude) / total_tx),
    ic_inf      = pmax(0, tasa_fraude - 1.96 * se),
    ic_sup      = tasa_fraude + 1.96 * se,
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

print(resumen_rafaga %>% select(ventana_rafaga, total_tx, pct_pob, tasa_fraude, lift))

ggplot(resumen_rafaga, aes(x = ventana_rafaga, y = tasa_fraude)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = lift > 2.0), alpha = 0.85, width = 0.65) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ic_inf, ymax = ic_sup), width = 0.2, color = "gray25") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tasa_global_fraude, linetype = "dashed", color = "red3", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(tasa_fraude, accuracy = 0.1)), vjust = -0.6, fontface = "bold", size = 3.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#2b5c8f", "TRUE" = "#d95f02"),
                    labels = c("Riesgo basal", "Alto riesgo (Lift > 2x)"),
                    name = "Nivel de Alerta") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.45)) +
  labs(title = "Efecto Ráfaga: Tasa de Fraude según Intervalo entre Ventas del Mismo Producto",
       subtitle = "Compras repetidas en < 10 minutos alcanzan un 34.8% de fraude (Lift 7x)",
       x = "Intervalo respecto a la última venta del mismo producto ('i')",
       y = "Tasa de Fraude") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# EVALUACIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA DE SCORING: CURVAS K-S Y PRECISION-RECALL (ESTILO MELI)
# ==============================================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# 1. Definición de Paleta Corporativa de Mercado Libre
col_amarillo_meli <- "#FFE600"
col_amarillo_osc  <- "#9A8400"
col_azul_oscuro   <- "#030C7D"
col_azul_claro    <- "#3483FA"
col_gris_linea    <- "gray70"

tema_meli <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 10),
    axis.title    = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.title  = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# 2. Separación de funciones acumuladas empíricas (ECDF) y K-S Stat
train_data <- df_limpio %>% filter(split == "train")

ecdf_0 <- ecdf(train_data$score[train_data$fraude == 0])
ecdf_1 <- ecdf(train_data$score[train_data$fraude == 1])
scores_u <- sort(unique(train_data$score))

data_ks <- tibble(
  score = scores_u,
  ecdf0 = ecdf_0(scores_u),
  ecdf1 = ecdf_1(scores_u),
  diferencia = abs(ecdf0 - ecdf1)
)

ks_max <- data_ks %>% filter(diferencia == max(diferencia)) %>% slice(1)
ks_val <- as.numeric(ks_max$diferencia)
ks_score <- as.numeric(ks_max$score)

p_ks <- ggplot(train_data, aes(x = score, color = factor(fraude))) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_segment(
    data = ks_max,
    aes(x = score, xend = score, y = ecdf0, yend = ecdf1),
    color = col_amarillo_osc, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.0,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = ks_score + 3, y = (ks_max$ecdf0 + ks_max$ecdf1) / 2,
    label = paste0("K-S Stat = ", percent(ks_val, accuracy = 0.1), "\n(Score = ", ks_score, ")"),
    color = col_amarillo_osc, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("0" = col_azul_oscuro, "1" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Legítima (Fraude = 0)", "Fraude (Fraude = 1)"),
    name = "Clase"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Gráfico K-S (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) sobre Score de Pasarela",
    subtitle = paste0("Máxima separación empírica entre legítimas y fraudes: ", percent(ks_val, accuracy = 0.1)),
    x = "Score de Riesgo (0 - 100)",
    y = "Proporción Acumulada (ECDF)"
  ) +
  tema_meli

# 3. Curva Precision-Recall del Score vs Línea de Azar (Prevalencia Basal)
prevalencia_train <- mean(train_data$fraude == 1)
thresholds_eval <- seq(0, 100, by = 1)

pr_curve_data <- map_dfr(thresholds_eval, function(th) {
  tp <- sum(train_data$score >= th & train_data$fraude == 1)
  fp <- sum(train_data$score >= th & train_data$fraude == 0)
  fn <- sum(train_data$score < th & train_data$fraude == 1)
  prec <- if_else(tp + fp == 0, 1.0, tp / (tp + fp))
  rec  <- tp / (tp + fn)
  tibble(threshold = th, precision = prec, recall = rec)
})

p_pr <- ggplot(pr_curve_data, aes(x = recall, y = precision)) +
  geom_line(color = col_azul_oscuro, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = prevalencia_train, linetype = "dotted", color = "red3", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 0.50, y = prevalencia_train + 0.04,
    label = paste0("Azar / Prevalencia Basal: ", percent(prevalencia_train, accuracy = 0.1)),
    color = "red3", fontface = "bold", size = 3.4
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1.02)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1.02)) +
  labs(
    title = "Curva Precision-Recall del Score Base vs. Azar",
    subtitle = "Muestra la elevación de precisión del scoring respecto a la prevalencia natural",
    x = "Recall (Cobertura de Fraude)",
    y = "Precisión (Aciertos Reales)"
  ) +
  tema_meli

# 4. Distribución Bimodal de Fraude (Violin Plot con Medias de Clase)
medias_score <- train_data %>%
  group_by(fraude) %>%
  summarise(media = mean(score), .groups = "drop")

p_violin <- ggplot(train_data, aes(x = factor(fraude), y = score, fill = factor(fraude))) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.75, width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = medias_score, aes(x = factor(fraude), y = media), color = "black", shape = 18, size = 4) +
  geom_text(
    data = medias_score,
    aes(x = factor(fraude), y = media, label = paste0("Media: ", round(media, 1))),
    vjust = -1.2, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = col_azul_claro, "1" = "#d95f02"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0" = "Legítima", "1" = "Fraude")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), limits = c(0, 110)) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución Bimodal de Fraude vs. Legítimas",
    subtitle = "Fraude concentra dos modas (score > 70 y cola oculta en score < 30)",
    x = "Tipo de Caso",
    y = "Score de Pasarela"
  ) +
  tema_meli

(p_ks + p_pr) / p_violin
```
